title: Touch Up Solutions
summary: A material-first catalog and how-to redesign for a repair-products business.
tagline: A redesign concept for a manufacturer of wood, leather, metal, and laminate repair products that organizes the catalog around the material a customer is repairing and puts how-to guides beside the products.
role: Designed and built the information architecture, pages, filters, cart experience, and visual system.

metrics.label: Pages designed and built
metrics.context: Catalog, material shops, guides, programs, videos, and resources.

problem: Touch Up Solutions makes repair products for many materials. That breadth is a strength in a showroom and an obstacle online: buyers arrive knowing the material and the job in front of them, but a broad catalog makes the right item hard to find.
contribution: I worked in Touch Up Solutions' warehouse from 2022 to 2024. For this redesign I designed and built the information architecture across 24 pages, a single catalog that feeds every category grid, filters, a persistent cart drawer, and the visual system.
solution: Browsing starts with the material: dedicated shops for wood and furniture, leather and vinyl, metal, and accessories, each with filters by product type. A how-to library sits beside the categories it applies to, and every guide links back to the right products. Separate Home User and Industrial User paths serve both kinds of customer.
solutionPoints: Material shops with filters for adhesives, burn-in sticks, fill sticks, markers, and more.
How-to guides for cabinets, furniture scratches, laminate flooring, burn-in tools, epoxy, and touch-up paint.
A quote request and quick-order path for trade buyers.
Dark walnut and cool-light surfaces with amber calls to action.

architecture.summary: One catalog feeds everything, and guides and products link in both directions.

decisions.title: Stay lightweight.
decisions.text: A catalog this size doesn't need heavy machinery; static pages load fast and are easy for the company's team to maintain.

decisions.title: One catalog feeds every page.
decisions.text: Adding or repricing a product is one change that appears wherever it is listed.

decisions.title: Link guides and products both ways.
decisions.text: A buyer who starts from a technique or from a product reaches the other in one click.

outcomes: The public preview demonstrates material-led discovery, product filters, and how-to content working together.
limits: This is a redesign preview, not the company's production store. The cart demonstrates the shopping flow; it is not presented as live payment processing.
lessons: Customers often search by the problem and material in front of them, not by a manufacturer's internal catalog structure.
